content:
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin, Python (scripting)
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [GITHUB]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7+ years of professional software development experience, building and operating services with Java and Kotlin. Experienced in REST API design, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS service environments. Has used Python for data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and is developing a Go CLI as a learning project. Interested in applying this backend experience in a role focused mainly on Python. Works in English and takes part in production on-call operations.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java, Kotlin; Python (scripts and small Jenkins helpers); Go (learning; side project)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, REST API design, OpenAPI 3, Spring Cloud Contract
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis, AWS S3, AWS SQS
Cloud and tools: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker, Jenkins
Testing and reliability: Testcontainers, contract testing, idempotent consumers, on-call incident response

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | 2022–Present
- Build and maintain Java and Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using Kafka and Kubernetes.
- Designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for insurance brokers; added partner-level rate limiting and Spring Cloud Contract tests. The API supports 12 broker partners and approximately 400,000 quote requests per month.
- Resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox pattern and idempotency keys for consumers. Duplicate claims fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
- Built the company’s first Kotlin service, an internal policy-PDF rendering service using Spring Boot, AWS S3 and SQS, and wrote Kotlin coding guidelines for the team.
- Participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rota. Handled a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024 and wrote a post-incident account that was praised.
- Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).
- Work in English.

Software Developer | Viajar Online | 2019–2021
- Worked on booking and payments in a large Java application.
- Raised payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer refactoring.
- Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot service, using RabbitMQ for messaging and Thymeleaf for templating.

SELECTED PROJECT
OpenAPI Diff CLI | Personal learning project | In progress
- Building a Go command-line tool to compare OpenAPI specifications; approximately 600 lines of code and not used in production.

CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer | 2020

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, honest, impact-oriented CV with a clear backend engineering profile. The quantified outcomes—400,000 quote requests per month, duplicate claims reduced from approximately 40 per week to zero, and test coverage increased from 35% to 70%—give the experience credibility and impact. The document is well structured, concise, and professionally written. It also handles the Python transition appropriately by clearly stating that Python experience is limited to scripts and Jenkins helpers rather than implying production Python service experience. The main content weakness is that several relevant capabilities appear only in the skills list rather than being connected to specific experience bullets, particularly PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS/cloud deployment, Jenkins/CI/CD, and technical trade-off communication.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The section headings, reverse-chronological structure, standard job titles, dates, and simple bullet formatting should parse well in most ATS platforms. The document contains relevant keywords including Java, Kotlin, Python, REST API, OpenAPI 3, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, EKS, AWS, automated testing, Jenkins, Spring Boot, and on-call incident response. AI screening should recognize a credible comparable-language match for the role, especially because the summary explicitly states interest in working mainly with Python. ATS alignment would improve if Jenkins were described more directly in relation to CI/CD and if PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS deployment, and cloud service operation were surfaced in the relevant experience bullets rather than relying mainly on the skills section. Do not add FastAPI, GitHub Actions, Terraform, observability tools, or production Python services because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the comparable-language backend requirement: the candidate has more than three years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and explicitly states interest in moving mainly toward Python. REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS services, Kafka, Kubernetes/EKS, automated testing, on-call operations, incident handling, and English-language work are all relevant to the role. The production reliability examples also fit the company’s emphasis on dependable services, ownership, and post-incident learning. The principal gaps are candidate-background gaps rather than document defects: the original material does not establish professional Python service development, PostgreSQL query tuning, or schema migrations. It also does not establish observability tooling, Terraform/infrastructure-as-code authorship, logistics or EDI experience, or Dutch/French language skills. The document does not show GitHub Actions specifically, although it does mention Jenkins-related work. The CV would be stronger by making the supported cloud, database, testing, CI/CD-adjacent, and trade-off experience more visible without overstating it.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the comparable-language qualification and Python scope slightly more explicit. For example, replace "Experienced in REST API design, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS service environments" with "Experienced in backend services using Java and Kotlin, with REST API design, PostgreSQL, Kafka, automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes/EKS, and AWS services." Retain the sentence clarifying that Python has been used for data-fix scripts and Jenkins helpers; do not imply production Python service experience.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Cloud and tools: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker, Jenkins" to "Cloud, deployment and CI/CD tools: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Kubernetes, Docker, Jenkins" so the role’s cloud deployment and CI/CD-adjacent keywords are easier for ATS screening to identify. Only use "CI/CD" as a label if the candidate is comfortable supporting that description; otherwise use "Build and delivery tools" and retain Jenkins.

3. In the Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, add the supported technologies to the relevant project bullets instead of leaving them only in Technical Skills. For example, revise the first bullet to "Build and maintain Java and Kotlin Spring Boot microservices deployed on Kubernetes (EKS), using PostgreSQL and Kafka." This makes the database, cloud, deployment, and event-streaming experience directly attributable to professional work.

4. In the Software Developer | Viajar Online experience section, revise the notifications bullet to include the supported Docker experience: "Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Dockerized Spring Boot service, using RabbitMQ for messaging and Thymeleaf for templating." This improves evidence for the Docker requirement without adding unsupported deployment claims.

5. In the Professional Experience section, make the technical trade-off evidence more explicit using facts already present. For example, revise the claims bullet to: "Resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by choosing a transactional outbox pattern and idempotency keys for consumers; duplicate claims fell from approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter." The wording should emphasize the engineering decision and reliability result, not claim formal architecture ownership beyond the documented work.

6. In the Tejo Insurance Tech on-call bullet, replace "wrote a post-incident account that was praised" with the more ATS- and recruiter-readable wording "wrote a post-incident report following a major Kafka lag incident in March 2024; the write-up was praised by the team." This more clearly connects the experience to incident investigation and post-mortem-style documentation while remaining truthful.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, focused CV with clear sections, credible technical detail, and several quantified outcomes. The API volume, duplicate-claim reduction, and test-coverage improvement provide convincing evidence of impact. It is appropriately transparent that Python has only been used for scripts and that Go is a learning project, avoiding overstatement. The main content limitation is that some relevant database and delivery experience appears only in the skills section rather than being connected to specific roles or projects. The wording in the summary is occasionally slightly awkward, particularly “Has used Python” and “AWS service environments.”
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional headings, simple text structure, standard date formatting, and searchable terms such as Java, Kotlin, Python, PostgreSQL, REST API, Kafka, Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Jenkins, automated testing, and CI/CD-adjacent tooling. AI screening probability is high for a comparable-language backend role, but moderate-to-high overall for this Python-focused vacancy because the CV explicitly shows no production Python service experience and does not contain FastAPI, query tuning, schema migrations, or a clearly stated CI/CD practice. Do not add unsupported Python frameworks or tools. The document should retain its honest distinction between Python scripting and production backend experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the comparable-language route in the advertisement: it demonstrates more than three years of professional backend development in Java/Kotlin, REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, Kafka, Kubernetes, automated testing, production on-call, and English-language collaboration. It also fits the company’s reliability culture through incident response, an incident account, idempotent consumers, and service ownership. The candidate's material shows gaps in production Python services, PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, REST API consumption, and explicit CI/CD ownership. Kubernetes is shown, but Terraform authoring is not. There is no evidence of observability tooling, logistics or EDI experience, or Dutch/French language skills. These are candidate-background gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The strongest alignment is for a backend engineer transitioning from Java/Kotlin into a mainly Python role, not for a candidate already experienced with Python/FastAPI in production.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace “Has used Python for data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers” with “Python experience includes data-fix scripts and small Jenkins automation helpers; production backend services have been built with Java and Kotlin.” This is more direct and preserves the important Python limitation.
2. In the Professional Summary, replace “AWS service environments” with “AWS services including EKS, S3 and SQS” so the cloud experience is concrete and easier for ATS and recruiters to interpret.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change “Cloud and tools: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker, Jenkins” to “Cloud and deployment: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Kubernetes (EKS), Docker; Automation: Jenkins helpers.” This accurately reflects the candidate’s use of Jenkins without implying unsupported ownership of a full CI/CD platform.
4. In the Tejo Insurance Tech experience section, add “using PostgreSQL” to the OpenAPI/API bullet or the claims/idempotency bullet, based on the documented project evidence. For example: “Designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for insurance brokers using PostgreSQL; added partner-level rate limiting and Spring Cloud Contract tests.” This connects the existing PostgreSQL skill to production experience.
5. In the Professional Summary, change “Works in English” to “Professional experience working in English, including backend guild meetings, production on-call communication and technical documentation.” This uses supported evidence and presents the language qualification more professionally.
